bank_name: Social Islami Bank PLC (Social Islami Bank Limited prior to 2022 name change; formerly Social Investment Bank Limited prior to 2009)
reporting_basis: SOLO / STANDALONE. Determined 2026-08-26 by matching this dataset's stored figures against the bank's own Solo-labeled financial statements, cross-checked five independent ways across the archive: (1) FY2010's own report presents both a 'CONSOLIDATED BALANCE SHEET' (Total Assets Taka 54,665,814,961) and a separate 'BALANCE SHEET' (Total Assets Taka 55,168,540,937) -- this dataset's stored FY2010 total assets (55,168.54m) is the Solo figure, not the Consolidated one; (2) the FY2012-FY2022 archive's recurring 'SIBL at a Glance' / '5 Years Key Financial Data' multi-year summary tables reproduce this dataset's stored figures for every overlapping year exactly; (3) the FY2018-FY2023 archive's 'Highlights of Performance' Annexure (Annexure-H / Annexure-I) is explicitly headed 'ONLY BANK-SOLO BASIS', and its figures (e.g. FY2018 Total Assets 307,305,321,444) match this dataset exactly; (4) FY2024's Note 16.5 is explicitly headed 'Capital Adequacy (Solo Basis)' as distinct from a separately-presented 'Capital Adequacy (Consolidated basis)' a few lines below it in the same note, and every FY2024 figure in this dataset (Total Eligible Capital 33,430,151,356; CRAR 6.43%; Total Tier I Capital 24,898,915,222) reproduces the Solo sub-table, not the Consolidated one (Consolidated Total eligible capital was 33,489,085,643 and Consolidated CRAR was also 6.43% to 2 d.p. but derived from a different RWA base of 521,134,540,732 vs Solo's 519,943,533,778); (5) SIBL has two wholly-owned subsidiaries consolidated throughout the archive (SIBL Securities Limited and SIBL Investment Limited, each 99.99% owned), so a Solo/Consolidated split exists in every year 2010-2024, and this dataset uses Solo throughout for consistency with the convention already used for other banks in this dataset (prefer Solo/Standalone; see _HANDOFF.md).
notes: annual_reports/SIBL archive covers 2010-2024 (15 text files, extracted by a prior session; sanity-checked here -- all 15 files are large (5,472 to 23,946 lines), none are empty/scanned stubs). Shariah-based Islamic bank: reports 'Investment' / 'Investments (General)' rather than conventional 'Loans and Advances', and 'Classified Investment' / 'Ratio of Classified Investments to Total Investments' rather than 'NPL' / 'NPL ratio' -- mapped to this dataset's gross_loans and npl_pct fields respectively, consistent with the convention already used for EXIMBANK, FIRSTSBANK and GIB in this dataset. Complete Q4/year-end coverage achieved for FY2010-FY2024 (15/15 years) from a combination of: each year's own Balance Sheet (Solo) and Profit and Loss Account (Solo) where directly extracted (FY2010, FY2011, FY2013, FY2015, FY2016, FY2024 in full; FY2012 partially); each year's own Capital Adequacy / Basel II-III disclosure (Tier-I/Tier-II/CRAR breakdown, extracted for every year FY2010-FY2024 without exception); and the recurring multi-year summary tables ('SIBL at a Glance' FY2012-FY2019 vintage, '5 Years Key Financial Data' FY2022/FY2024 vintage, 'Highlights of Performance' Annexure-H/I FY2018-FY2023 vintage), cross-checked against overlapping reports. Only Q4/year-end (audited) data was extracted; Q1/H1/Q3 unaudited interim data was not researched (see the dedicated source entry below). UPDATE 2026-08-26: FY2025 was researched and confirmed unavailable -- Social Islami Bank PLC was declared a failed/non-viable institution and placed under resolution, then absorbed into the newly formed state-owned Sammilito Islami Bank PLC together with four other crisis-hit Shariah banks (EXIM Bank, First Security Islami Bank, Global Islami Bank, Union Bank), all five already confirmed in this dataset to have no FY2025 annual report for the same reason. See the '2025 (Q4)' entry below for the full evidence trail. This bank's independent standalone-reporting series ends at FY2024.

sources.note: Fully extracted from FY2024's own primary financial statements; all four validation checks (balance-sheet identity, Tier1+Tier2=Total Capital, PBT-tax=PAT, classified%-reproduction) pass exactly to the Taka. MAJOR FINDING -- QUALIFIED AUDIT OPINION WITH MATERIAL UNCERTAINTY: see the FY2024 quarterly JSON's period_note for the full citation trail. In summary: Bangladesh Bank letter DBI-7/4(2)/2025-346 (29-Apr-2025) required provisions of Tk 23,158.06 crore against Tk 1,502.62 crore maintained (+ Tk 78.18 crore paid); Bangladesh Bank letter DOS(CAMS)1157/41(Dividend)/2025-3109 (21-May-2025) permitted finalizing without the shortfall (forbearance); the Auditors' Material Uncertainty paragraph states CRAR would fall from the reported 6.43% to NEGATIVE 33.95% if the deferred shortfall were recognized, implying a Tk 22,850.14 crore total capital shortfall against the 12.50% requirement. AT LEAST FOUR further, non-reconciled shortfall figures appear elsewhere in the same audited report (Tk 20,993.72 crore per Note 7.8 and Note 16.5's footnote identically; Tk 21,626.58 crore and a 'permitted' Tk 21,577.26 crore per Note 14.11's footnote citing the same two BB letters; Tk 21,655.44 crore per the Directors' Report) -- none reconciled to each other or to the Auditors'-Report figures; all recorded verbatim in the quarterly JSON's period_note per this project's never-silently-reconcile convention. FY2024 is also the first reported net loss (PAT -532.74m Solo; DSE's disclosure table separately shows a larger Consolidated loss of -1,017.03m) in this dataset's SIBL series, and RWA nearly doubled year-on-year (305,922.96m to 519,943.53m) despite near-flat total-asset growth (+0.07%), consistent with credit-risk-weight escalation from the asset-quality collapse (classified-investment ratio 4.79% to 61.74%).

sources.notes: No FY2025 (year ended 31 December 2025) annual report or standalone audited financial statements exist for Social Islami Bank as an independent entity, confirmed via a time-boxed check across three independent channels (approx. 15-20 minutes of research, consistent with this dataset's precedent for the other four banks in the same merger): (1) DSE's own dynamically-updated company page (dsebd.org/displayCompany.php?name=SIBL, fetched via curl due to a WebFetch TLS-certificate error on the domain) shows the 'Financial Performance as per Audited Financial Statements' table stopping at FY2024 (EPS -0.89 consolidated, NAV/share 18.15, Profit for the year -1,017.03m -- all consistent with this dataset's independently-sourced FY2024 Solo figures), and its 'Interim Financial Performance: 2025' table shows populated quarterly EPS through Q3 2025 (Q1 -1.410, Half-Yearly cumulative -4.330, 9-Months cumulative -15.280, market price collapsing from Tk 10.1 to Tk 4.4 over the year) with the 'Annual' column explicitly blank ('-') for every row -- the same 'quarterly data continues, annual column stays blank' signature already documented for EXIMBANK and GIB; (2) a Wayback Machine CDX search of siblbd.com's report-hosting paths (annual_report/*, assets/reports/annual/*, assets/reports/annual_statements/*; ~110 report-related URLs found across all naming conventions used over the site's history) finds 'SIBL_Annual_Report_2024.pdf' and 'Annual_Financial_Statements_2024.pdf' as the latest crawled annual filings under every tested naming convention, with no 2025-year file of any kind; (3) SIBL's own live homepage (siblbd.com, fetched 2026-08-26) has itself been rebranded and now identifies the institution as 'Sammilito Islami Bank PLC', referencing an 11th Board of Directors meeting of 'Sammilito Islami Bank PLC, a state-owned Shariah-based bank' dated 25 August 2026 (the day before this retrieval) -- the single strongest piece of evidence found across this dataset's five merged-bank investigations, since it is the bank's own current self-identification rather than a third-party report. REASON: per WebSearch results (The Daily Star, BSS News, Wikipedia's 'Sammilito Islami Bank' article), Social Islami Bank PLC was declared a failed/non-viable institution and placed under resolution under the Bank Resolution Ordinance 2025, then merged into a newly formed state-owned entity, Sammilito Islami Bank PLC, together with four other crisis-hit Shariah banks already confirmed in this dataset to have no FY2025 report for the identical reason (EXIM Bank, First Security Islami Bank, Global Islami Bank, Union Bank). Bangladesh Bank issued a Letter of Intent and no-objection certificate for Sammilito Islami Bank on 9 November 2025 (before FY2025/Dec-2025 had even closed); press coverage variously describes Sammilito Islami Bank beginning operations in early December 2025 and, per the concurrently-researched GIB/EXIMBANK sessions in this dataset, 18 August 2026 as a date associated with the transition to fully independent (non-administrator-led) operations -- the exact operational-handover date differs slightly across sources and was not further reconciled, as it does not change the conclusion. CONCLUSION: this is a confirmed, permanent series-end for SIBL as an independently reporting entity, not an ordinary reporting lag. Total time spent on this FY2025 investigation: approximately 20 minutes (one WebSearch, two WebFetch calls, one DSE curl fetch, one Wayback CDX pass), consistent with the task's time-boxing instruction given the strong prior expectation from the other four merged banks already in this dataset.

sources.period: 2010-2024 (embedded quarterly-performance tables in own annual reports)
notes: Per this dataset's standing 'mine already-downloaded annual-report text first' rule: grepped all 15 files in annual_reports/SIBL/*.txt for the BSEC-mandated quarterly-disclosure heading and its variants. Found TWO distinct embedded tables, present in most (not all) years: (a) 'Significant variance in operating results between Quarterly and Annually' / 'Variance Analysis -- Quarterly and Annually' -- an income-statement-only cumulative Q1/H1/9M/Annual table (Investment Income, Profit Paid on Deposits, Net Investment Income, Income from Shares, Commission/Exchange/Brokerage, Other Operating Income, Total Operating Income, Operating Expenses, Salaries, Other Opex, Operating Profit before provisions & taxes), present with genuine data in FY2013-FY2022 and FY2024 (not FY2010-FY2012, not FY2023 [present but severely OCR-corrupted/unreadable], not FY2011); (b) 'Comparative Analysis of Capital maintained throughout the year' -- a quarterly Capital Requirement/Maintained/Tier-1/Tier-2/RWA/CRAR table, present only in FY2010, FY2012, FY2013, FY2014 (discontinued in later annual reports). VALUE ASSESSMENT: this table only ever provides INCOME-STATEMENT and (for 4 years only) CAPITAL data -- never a quarterly Balance Sheet snapshot (no quarterly Total Assets/Deposits/Investments/Equity anywhere in any annual report) -- so it could not, by itself, produce a CITYBANK-schema-equivalent quarterly file. It was used instead as (i) a preview of expected figures before fetching SIBL's own quarterly PDF archive, and (ii) a cross-validation source once the PDFs were fetched: every income-statement figure checked this way (dozens of cross-checks, e.g. 2024 Q1 Investment Income 7,087.49m / Net Investment Income 1,557.80m / Total Operating Income 2,515.42m / Operating Profit 626.60m, all matching the interim PDF's own Solo P&L exactly) matched the primary-source interim PDF, and confirmed FY2024's Q3-alone (Jul-Sep) pre-provision operating profit was already NEGATIVE (Q3 cumulative 1,185.77m < Q2 cumulative 1,686.08m) -- see insights.json. Where the two sources disagreed by a small, consistent margin (a few percent, e.g. FY2013/FY2014 Q1), the gap is explained by this table being Solo-basis while several years' own interim PDF was Consolidated-only (see the reporting_basis field and each quarter's own period_note) -- not a data error.

sources.notes: SIBL's own 'Quarterly/Half-yearly Statements' tab (distinct from its 'Annual Reports' and 'Annual Financial Statements' tabs on the same page) lists 43 items spanning Q3 2012/H1 2012 through Q3 2025 (41 PDFs + 2 JPG newspaper-disclosure images for a 2021 Q3/Q2 compliance ad, not used). Verified still live and working as of 2026-08-27 (re-confirmed via a raw HTML href scrape, not just a WebFetch summary, to rule out truncation). Downloaded all 41 PDFs directly from this archive (base URL https://www.siblbd.com/assets/reports/quarterly_halfyearly/), extracted with pdftotext -layout, OCR'd (pdftoppm 300dpi + tesseract) the 9 that had no extractable text layer, deleted all PDFs after extraction per project policy. 37 of the 41 quarters yielded usable, validated data; 4 did not (see the two 'unavailable' entries below). Reporting basis is per-quarter, not uniform across the whole archive: SIBL's own interim filings presented CONSOLIDATED ONLY (no separate Solo statement at all) for every quarter FY2012 H1 through FY2015, plus FY2016 Q1 and FY2017 Q1 specifically; a separate SOLO statement has been presented alongside the Consolidated one from FY2016 Q2 onward (FY2017 Q1 is a one-off reversion back to Consolidated-only, then Solo resumes from FY2017 Q2). Where only Consolidated was available, it is used and flagged per this dataset's convention (30 of 37 quarters are Solo-basis, matching the main Q4/annual series; 6 are Consolidated-only [2013 Q1, 2014 Q1-Q3, 2015 Q1-Q3, 2016 Q1, 2017 Q1 -- 8 quarters total across that list]; FY2012 Q2 predates the Solo/Consolidated distinction being drawn at all and is recorded as 'unlabeled' basis; 2022 Q2 is a MIXED-basis exception -- see its own dedicated note below). Capital adequacy (CRAR/Tier-1/Tier-2/RWA) and classified-investment/NPL figures are NOT disclosed in ANY interim filing checked in this archive (confirmed absent, not a parsing gap) -- SIBL only discloses these annually.

sources.notes: Extraction: pdftotext -layout for 32 of 41 PDFs; pdftoppm (300dpi) + tesseract OCR for 9 that had no extractable text layer (2012 Q3 [see unavailable entry], 2020 Q1 [see unavailable entry], 2020 Q2, 2021 Q1, 2021 Q3, 2022 Q1, 2022 Q3, plus 2 more attempted for the two unavailable quarters). All 41 downloaded PDFs were deleted after extraction per project policy; no PDFs or extracted raw-text files were retained in the repository -- only the resulting structured quarterly/*.json files and this sources.json entry's provenance metadata (matching this dataset's 'only structured data, source URLs/metadata, and provenance are kept long-term' rule). Validation: (1) balance-sheet identity (Total Assets = Total Liabilities + Total Equity) checked for all 37 quarters, passing to within rounding (typically 0-2 Taka, i.e. non-controlling-interest rounding) in every case; (2) a second-pass internal-consistency audit checking that Net Investment Income + Income from Shares + Commission + Other Operating Income sums to Total Operating Income, and that Total Operating Income minus Expenses minus Provision minus Tax chains arithmetically to Net Profit After Tax -- this second pass caught extraction defects in 11 of the 37 quarters that the balance-sheet-identity check alone had missed (see each affected quarter's own note above and each affected line item's own metric_note); (3) cross-validation against DSE's own 'Interim Financial Performance: 2025' disclosure table for FY2025 EPS, and against this bank's own embedded FY2024 annual-report quarterly-performance table for FY2024 Q1-Q3 income-statement figures -- both matched exactly. A DATA-INTEGRITY TRAP specific to this session's shared scratch environment: two PDFs downloaded fresh from SIBL's own site (2012 Q3, 2013 Q2) and re-derived pdftotext output later re-read for OCR purposes (2013 Q3, 2020 Q1) were found, upon re-inspection, to have been silently overwritten on local disk by an unrelated, concurrently-running research session working on a different bank (Standard Bank Limited) that happened to reuse the exact same generic scratch filenames -- caught only because this dataset independently verifies the bank-identity header text of every source page rather than trusting a filename. This affected only local scratch-directory files, never anything in this repository; it is recorded here as a general caution for any future session reusing generic scratch filenames for PDF downloads in a shared environment.
